headline: World No 81 Sykes knocks out Humphries 10-9
standfirst: Tom Sykes broke the second seed’s throw in a deciding leg to reach his first major quarter-final, while Luke Humphries revealed he had played through a shoulder injury.
body: Tom Sykes, ranked 79 places below Luke Humphries, is into the quarter-finals of the Grand Slam of Darts after breaking the world No 2’s throw in the final leg of a 10-9 win in Wolverhampton on Thursday. On his debut at the event, it is the first major quarter-final we have on record for him.

The decider should have been Humphries’ leg. He had the throw and had taken three of the previous four legs, two of them in 11 darts, to level at 9-9. He then missed a match dart at double 10, and Sykes stepped in to take out 36 in 13 darts.

He had to win it twice. Sykes led 4-0 after an 11-dart fourth leg, only for Humphries to take six of the next seven and lead 6-5. Sykes answered with a three-leg run, including a 114 checkout to break throw, to go 8-6 up.

Humphries averaged 102.02, the higher of the two, and still lost. Sykes made up the difference elsewhere: eight 180s to four, 43.5 per cent on his doubles to 37.5, and five breaks of throw. His 99.32 average was more than five points above the 93.75 he has managed over the last 12 months.

Sykes, now guaranteed £35,000, plays Michael van Gerwen on Saturday at 7:15pm. Humphries said afterwards he had been struggling with a trapped nerve in his right shoulder, but did not use it as an excuse.
